headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file prompt injection and data leakage are limited by both agents' lack of filesystem/network access, but the pair still has an indirect content-to-content pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is an open-source awesome-list with no runtime isolation details, while B can process audio/speech files and has no provenance controls. There is no direct shared channel in the profiles, but if A’s content is copied into B’s inputs or a shared workspace is introduced, B could treat attacker-controlled text as authoritative. Uncertainty about the bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A's content is copied into B's transcription input or prompt context
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is introduced between the pair
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Do not paste A-generated text into B without review
Add a provenance label to any text passed from A to B
requires-engineering: add input sanitization/provenance checks in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress; B touches audio/speech but also has no network egress and cannot read filesystems. With no shared workspace or outbound transmission, leakage is constrained to local handling of audio files, so the blast radius is small. The pair still warrants caution because the profiles are docs-only and unverified.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted between A and B
IF either agent is wrapped by an external uploader or logging pipeline
mitigations: Delete temporary audio files after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or git capabilities in the profile, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write surface, a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is replaced with a writable or git-modifying variant
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable directory
requires-engineering: add lockfiles if write access is later enabled

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume files and produce speech transcripts, so if A’s outputs are fed into B as source material, B may render them without independent verification. A is an awesome-list rather than a fact engine, which lowers but does not remove the risk of downstream over-trust. The interaction is indirect and undocumented, so uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF A's text is used as source content for B's transcription or summarization workflow
IF B is configured to publish outputs without human review
mitigations: Require human review before publishing B's output
Mark A-derived content as untrusted source material
Separate source content from generated output in filenames
requires-engineering: add verification steps before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes, and B only lists audio/speech with no stated regulated-data handling, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced
